newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge sees higher metals prices.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge sees higher metals prices.

text.p: Nickel giant Falconbridge Ltd said on Friday it expects higher prices for nickel and copper in the coming year.
If demand for nickel increases by one or two percent, the world nickel price should react, Joe Laezza, vice-president of marketing and sales, told an analysts' conference call.
"The prospect of a major increase in supply is unlikely," he said.
A surplus of stainless steel in 1996 had kept the nickel price in check so far this year, Laezza said.
Stainless steel consumes about 60 percent of world nickel.
"The general malaise of the stainless steel market has been bad, and has spread through the whole industry," said Laezza.
But stainless steel stockpiles are shrinking, he said.
Laezza said he also expects the copper price to rise as high as US$1 a pound in the first months of 1997 from its current level of US$0.89 per pound.
"I think there's still some steam left in copper," he said.
Falconbridge blamed low metal prices for the poor third quarter results it released Friday.
The company earned C$30.1 million or C$0.17 a share before extraordinary gains, down from C$84.5 million or C$0.47 a share a year earlier.
Capital expenditures so far this year amount to about C$400 million and are expected to rise to C$700 by the end of the year, chief executive Alex Balogh said in the conference call.
He expects capital expenditures in 1997 to total between C$800 million and C$850 million.
"A big piece of this is Collahuasi," he said.
The company has said it hopes to begin production at the Chilean copper project by January 1999.
